|Choose it when
|you need a random number an attacker must not predict; never `std::mt19937` or `rand` (link:https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/338.html[CWE-338, a weak generator used for security])
|you compare anything secret; never `==` or `memcmp` on a MAC
|you branch on a failure: forged data, a wrong size, no entropy
|a key goes to or comes from a file, a form or a tool as `-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----` text; with the `encode_spki` and `encode_pkcs8` of `curves::ed25519`, `curves::x25519`, `curves::secp256k1` or `curves::p256`
|a native program on OpenSSL must allocate only from its own arena; on WebAssembly, BearSSL allocates nothing
|a key pair signs with `sign(scheme, input)` and a signature is checked with `verify(scheme, signature, input, public_key)`; a digest computed elsewhere, such as a Bitcoin sighash, goes in marked as `prehashed`, never as a bare span
|a template takes any curve's key pair: `make`, `generate`, a typed `public_key()` that `verify` takes, `secret()`, and `sign(scheme, input)`
